evidence: Phaedr. 1.10.4: lupus arguēbat vulpem fūrtī crīmine
terms.comment: To bring charges against someone: crīmina alicuī īnferre (Traupman 194).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the accusative of the person and the genitive or ablative of the charge
terms.comment: aliquem crīmine (or dē crīmine, crīminis) arguere (Traupman 194).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, with the accusative of the person and the genitive or dē of the charge
evidence: Publil. Sent. N 25: Nēminem citō accūsāverīs
terms.comment: Of a formal accusation, and of finding fault in general.

terms.grammar: phrase: reus, reī m. (the accused) with facere and the accusative of the person

phrases.latin: lupus arguēbat vulpem fūrtī crīmine; negābat illa sē esse culpae proximam
phrases.english: the wolf charged the fox with theft; she denied that she was anywhere near guilty

phrases.latin: Difficilem habēre oportet aurem ad crīmina.
phrases.english: one should have an ear that is slow to listen to accusations

sources: Lewis & Short: crimen · Lewis & Short: arguo · Lewis & Short: accuso · Lewis & Short: reus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 193–194, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
